rows.evidence: Q1: Section 2.6 and Fig. 1 report the authors' own new data on bean yields over three harvests of C. arabica cv. Catua<U+00ED> under FACE (elevated vs ambient CO2) in Brazil, n=10 <U+00B1> SE.
rows.notes: The paper is mainly a review but includes one new dataset (FACE yields). It contains no evidence on drip or sensor-based irrigation: the FACE trial was explicitly rain-fed/unirrigated, and its own result is that elevated CO2 raised coffee yields by ~28% and may mitigate heat effects. Irrigation is mentioned only in passing (Verhage et al. assumption that irrigation use remains the same; a speculative remark that CO2 benefits may be larger in intensive systems 'including irrigation'). No own result on efficient irrigation as climate-risk adaptation.
